memo: Base: the pipeline embedded in sanpier's 'Candidate-aware PubChem promotion 0.465' (frozen_0465 = dmitriigluzdov 'CASMI 26: The Data Behind Spectra to Structures' v16 + sanpier's rank-1 PubChem promotion), kernels/e3/base_f465.ipynb, + ours own COCONUT + lfrag (e3f465oc-1, LB 0.467, our best). New part (ours, 10-27): leak-free engine-1 ranker. Our validation kernel yasunorim/casmi26-e3rk0 held 800 enveda-180 molecules of dmitriigluzdov's identity fold 0 out of train (c1: other-library spectra kept; c2: all removed), swapped the engine FP to the fold-safe fpnet_fold0 and dumped the public ranker's 160 input features for the top 300 candidates + truth. A LightGBM lambdarank refit on these rows (5-fold CV by molecule) beats the public ranker on the same molecules: MRR@25 0.926 -> 0.981 (c1 0.864 -> 0.971; 80 molecules up, 4 down); without the FPNet A/B/D 'model_views' features (which saw the molecules) still 0.967 (67 up, 15 down). Here the booster is fitted in-kernel on all rows WITHOUT the 7 model_views features (FPNet A/B/D saw the held-out molecules, so their weight in the refit may be a leak) and replaces the public ranker (rknew=1 rknomv=1); pair to e3f465rk-1 (all features). Hypothesis: the public ranker was fitted on rows where each molecule's own spectra were in the library, so it under-weights matches from other instruments, which is the hidden test's class 1 (timsTOF queries, references from other instruments); LB >= 0.475. Effect size: 8-10% of molecules move up in the simulation; even a fifth of that on the hidden 400 is +6 molecules. build.py f465rm base=f465 ownco=1 lfrag=1 rknew=1 rknomv=1.
message: e3f465rm-1: f465 + own COCONUT + lfrag (0.467) + our leak-free refit of the engine-1 ranker without the FPNet A/B/D view features
